newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads tighten a tad.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds sag, spreads tighten a tad.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed security prices edged lower, but some yield spreads to Treasuries tightened a tad in thin trade on Thursday, traders said.
"Mortgage (spreads) are tighter again today," said one head mortgage trader at a large U.S. investment bank in New York.
He said customers continued to scoop up most coupons across the spectrum with particular interest in Ginnie Mae and Fannie Mae 8.0-percent coupons.
Despite the light buying, prices of Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 11/32 at 100-06/32 bid, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 7/32 at 100-04/32 and Freddie Mac paper was down 8/32 at 100-09/32.
Mortgage bankers unloaded 7.0 percent coupons into a thinly supplied market, said another pass-through trader. And buyers quickly digested the new supply, he said.
"Overall, issuance has been very low," said Cynthia Rivera, a mortgage research analyst at BZW Securities Inc.
Spreads will not necessarily widen when mortgage bankers sell, Rivera said, because there is perceived to be lots of demand.
In Treasury trading, the five-year Treasury note was off 6/32 to yield 6.36 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was off 11/32, yielding 6.49 percent.
